open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove or refute a parameter-uniform bound \(B\) on the number of common constant-hazard pieces needed by exact optimizers when both nuisance hazards are saturated and the two remaining controls may follow repeated alternating four-corner cycles; then assemble this with flat, singular, abnormal, and boundary regimes.
open_obligations.obstruction: Compactness proves existence of a measurable optimizer but supplies no uniform switching complexity. The switching-function derivatives bound the nuisance switches, yet in the phase \(z=w=1\) with both factual-incidence multipliers negative they permit repeated \((0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)\) cycles. Neither endpoint dimension nor piecewise-constant approximation preserves the four factual endpoint equalities and the support objective exactly, and no cycle-deletion inequality or optimal repeated-cycle counterexample has been certified.
open_obligations.attempted: The mandated two-cycle word was evaluated by exact elementary exponential recursions. At the equal-duration feasible point its constraint Jacobian has rank five and the explicit tangent in the partial result changes the objective with both signs, so that point is not a stationary obstruction and a constrained Hessian test there is inapplicable. Single-control singular intervals were exactly pulse-compressed. Direct switching-function and bracket calculations exclude the proposed simultaneous interior singular candidate as a source of an optimizer, but they do not bound the number of alternating bang cycles. Finite-grid and restricted-family calculations were not used as global certificates.
